current.title: You'd Guess Indonesia. The Data Says Otherwise.
current.hook: Your guess was wrong: the US has 165 volcanoes, and Indonesia has only 101.
current.closing: Alaska: quietly winning at volcanoes since forever.
current.question: Seen a volcano in person? Where?

segments.say: The US has 165 volcanoes active in 11,700 years; Japan has 118, Russia 107, Indonesia 101.
130 of those 165 sit in Alaska alone; without Alaska, the US barely registers.
All four sit on the Ring of Fire, which holds 75% of Earth's volcanoes.

judge.one_line: A chart slideshow with wrong titles and a nonsensical '50% apart' closing. The story's real payoff (Alaska alone beats every country) is never shown.
problems: The hook is a static ranked list of cloned Datas. Indonesia is not visibly 'beaten' with any motion beyond the rows sliding.
Titles contradict the content: 'Indonesia's volcano rank' over a US-led list (seg0, seg1), 'Indonesia versus Alaska' over Alaska vs rest of US (seg2), 'Indonesia's Ring of Fire' (seg3).
seg1: the bar label 'United States o...' is truncated, the 165 is covered by Data's hand, the map label is clipped at the left edge, and the captions show '101. / 107' out of sync with the narration.
seg2: Data is cut off at the frame's left edge and just holds a pole while volcanoes stack themselves. A stray volcano floats in empty sky.
seg3: two bare bubbles reading 75%/25%. A bare number card with no Ring of Fire picture.
seg4: the closing ruler reads '50% apart', which is meaningless for the story, and 'On the Ring of Fire 75%' overprints 'Everywhere else on Earth 25%'.
fixes: Make the hook an action: Data yanks the Indonesia volcano off the top spot and the US volcano stack erupts past it in the first second.
Retitle each scene to what it shows (e.g. 'Who has the most volcanoes?', 'Alaska vs the rest of the US').
seg1: widen the label column or abbreviate to 'United States', keep Data off the value label, and sync captions to the numbers spoken.
seg2: bring Data fully into frame and have him load the volcano cones onto the Alaska pan himself, so his work tips the scale.
seg3: draw the Pacific Ring of Fire as a ring of volcano cones around an ocean, with 75% of the cones lit on the ring vs 25% scattered elsewhere.
seg4: replace the gap ruler with an Alaska payoff (130 cones in one heap towering over the other countries' piles). One number, no overlapping labels.

rules: TITLE or HOOK must contain a consequential NUMBER from the data below (the gate refuses a title+hook with no digit in either).

TITLE must be a PREMISE, not a searchable noun phrase: more than five words, or a number, or a question mark, or a tension word. 'Oldest Written Languages' is the failure; 'Why 3 of the 5 Oldest Scripts Are Still Unreadable' is the shape.

Every segment's TOPIC (a 2-4 word on-screen label) must share at least one real word with the TITLE — the gate checks a keyword bridge from each segment to the headline. Rename the topic, or write the title so it names what the segments are about.

Every NUMBER you say in a segment's SAY must be one that segment's data can show: a listed value, a difference between two of them, a percent change, a share of the total, or the same value in a bigger unit. A number from nowhere is refused — a guard derives every spoken quantity from the listed points.
Keep every number that is already correct. Do not add a country, company or person the data does not name.

PACE: each SAY is ONE spoken sentence of at most 16 words — the number and what it means, nothing else; the HOOK at most 14 words, the CLOSING at most 10, the QUESTION at most 8. A beat is on screen about 8 seconds; a longer line is refused. Each SAY says its beat's headline number out loud.

Each beat is part of a STORY, not a readout: one number a beat (two only for a then-and-now), said with what it means. Name no group a viewer would not know ('the experts', not 'the OECD'); the WHO, NASA and the White House are fine.
TOPIC labels are printed on the video: at most 4 words, no clause.

The HOOK is clickbait, never a scam: the most surprising TRUE fact in the story, 5-14 words, said the way a person tells a friend. It makes sense heard once. 'You' only when it is the viewer's own money, body or kids. No formula tags ('...and nobody told you', '...shocking everyone'), no quiz ('Which animal...', 'Did you know...'), no hedge (might, may), no vague size ('astonishing'). Exaggerate nothing.

how_to_answer: Rewrite the WORDS so this story clears every rule above and answers every reason in `held_for`. Same number of segments, same order. Use ONLY numbers you can derive from each segment's `data.points` (or a year that appears as a label). If `judge` is present, its `problems`/`fixes` are what the video editor saw on the RENDERED video — shorter topics and one clear number per line are what fix 'unreadable' and 'text on text'.
